title: Spin-to-polarization mapping with a coherent quantum dot-cavity receiver
authors: Adrià Medeiros, Vincent Vinel, Eliott Rambeau, Petr Steindl, Elham Mehdi, Manuel Gundín, Clément Millet, Petr Stepanov, Niccolo Somaschi, Aristide Lemaître, Isabelle Sagnes, Olivier Krebs, Pascale Senellart, Dario A. Fioretto, Loïc Lanco
abstract: Coherent light-matter interfaces controllably modifying the state of a photon upon interaction with a stationary qubit are a key resource for implementing deterministic entangling gates for optical quantum technologies. This requires a one-to-one mapping between the state of the scattered photon and that of the embedded qubit. Here, we present an experimental signature of such a bijection by leveraging the spin-induced Kerr rotation present in a low-noise charged quantum dot-micropillar cavity device. Through time-resolved polarization measurements, we project the electron spin to one of its eigenstates with $95\pm2\%$ fidelity with a single reflected photon detection, and follow the subsequent spin relaxation through the detection of a second reflected photon. We demonstrate that, after a transient regime governed by the trion radiative lifetime, two orthogonal polarization states can be produced, each associated to a given spin eigenstate. While the current results are limited by a timescale competition between electron spin relaxation and trion radiative lifetime, they could be improved using hole spins displaying increased relaxation times. Our work paves the way towards deterministic logic gates exploiting this one-to-one mapping between a spin and the polarization of a scattered photon.
summary: This experimental work demonstrates a method to deterministically map the spin state of an electron in a quantum dot onto the polarization state of a reflected photon. By leveraging spin-induced Kerr rotation in a QD-cavity system, the authors achieve high-fidelity spin projection and show that the spin relaxation dynamics can be read out via subsequent photon polarization measurements. This paves the way for building quantum logic gates using solid-state emitters.
main_problem: The paper aims to experimentally demonstrate a deterministic, one-to-one mapping (bijection) between the spin state of an embedded electron and the polarization state of a scattered photon.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated this spin-to-polarization mapping using a charged quantum dot-cavity device, showing that two orthogonal polarization states can be generated, each corresponding to a specific spin eigenstate.
method: Time-resolved polarization measurements are used to project the electron spin onto its eigenstates and subsequently track spin relaxation dynamics via the detection of a second reflected photon.
model_or_system: The physical system is a negatively-charged InGaAs Quantum Dot embedded in an AlGaAs micropillar cavity. The mechanism relies on the spin-induced Kerr rotation within this QD-cavity structure.
key_observables: Spin projection fidelity ($95\pm2\%$), the relative angle ($\alpha$) between Stokes vectors ($\vec{S}|\phi_1 \approx -\vec{S}| ar{\phi}_1$), and the conditional Stokes parameter $s_{\phi ar{\phi}}^{|\phiangle}(	au)$.
important_parameters: The experiment is limited by the timescale competition between electron spin relaxation ($T_{	ext{spin}}^{-1} \approx 1.9$ ns) and the trion radiative lifetime ($T_{	ext{rad}}^{-1} \approx 200$ ps).
main_assumptions: The initial model assumes the low-power limit and neglects decoherence for optical transitions or spin states, though the analysis tracks relaxation dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy levels and the dependence of the polarization overlap on detuning ($\Delta\omega$), and show the evolution of the conditional Stokes parameter $s_{\phi ar{\phi}}^{|\phiangle}(	au)$ over time delay $	au$.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework for the spin-photon mapping using Kerr rotation, details the measurement protocol involving conditional polarization tomography, presents the quantitative results showing spin projection fidelity, and discusses the limitations imposed by relaxation timescales.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the realization of quantum logic gates by establishing a robust physical mechanism (spin-photon coupling) for deterministic quantum state transfer, which is central to quantum information processing.

Spintronics.note: The experimental demonstration of mapping electron spin state to photon polarization using a QD-cavity structure directly addresses the interface between quantum optics and spin physics, specifically involving spin-induced effects in a cavity QED setting.
